about: A <history> records what its parent held when the parent was left, and entering it brings that back. `running` has a shallow history `last` and a deep one `deepest`; `working` has a deep one `crew_all` over a <parallel> of two regions. Resumed through `last` the machine enters `fast` and takes its initial child `cruise`, through `deepest` it lands in the atomic state it left, and through `crew_all` it stands in both regions at once. A step's `configuration` is the set of every active state, a compound or a parallel one with the atomic ones below it, by the id the document gives it; the order is not part of the answer. The history is recorded again each time its parent is left, so the second `deepest` resume lands where the machine was the second time. A plain entry of `working` ignores the history and starts at the initial children. Expected values are derived from the document and the history rules, not observed from a backend.

steps.note: `fast` is entered with its initial child
the deep history brings back the atomic state it left, below `fast`
the shallow history brings back only the child that was active, `fast`, which takes its initial child: `cruise` and not `burst`; the transition counted the resume
`running` is left from `cruise`: `last` records [fast] again and `deepest` now records [cruise]
the deep history was recorded again by that exit, so it lands in `cruise` this time
`running` is left; nothing of it is held now
`working` is entered through its initial child, a <parallel> that starts every region in its first child
`working` is left: `crew_all` records the atomic state of each region, [l2, r2]
the deep history of a <parallel> brings both regions back at once
a plain entry of `working` does not consult its history: both regions start over
